title: Exploring the world of edge-chromatic 3-critical graphs
summary: A graph $G$ with maximum degree $Δ$ is $Δ$-critical if it is connected, satisfies $χ'(G)=Δ+1$, and the deletion of any edge reduces its chromatic index to $Δ$. A $Δ$-critical graph $G$ is called nontrivial if it contains no $Δ$-overfull subgraph; that is, no $H \subseteq G$ such that $|E(H)| > Δ\lfloor |V(H)| /2 \rfloor$. There are no $1$-critical graphs, and the $2$-critical graphs are exactly the odd cycles.
